rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two names for the mountain passes have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: هما بمعنى واحد , وقيل : المضموم من فعل الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative assigns the damma form to God's action and the fatha form to people's action.
rows.anchor: المضموم من فعل الله , والمفتوح من فعل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people lived near the two passes on the side nearest the direction from which Dhul-Qarnayn came.
rows.anchor: أي بقربهما من الجانب الذي هو أدنى منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were strong people whose language was extremely distant from other languages because their land was remote.
rows.anchor: أي أقوياء لغتهم في غاية البعد من لغات بقية الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they could scarcely understand Dhul-Qarnayn well; they managed only with much effort because neither side had a skilled interpreter.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقربون من أن يفهموه ممن ذي القرنين فهما جيدا كما يفهم غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their difficulty implies vast wilderness separated them from other populations, explaining why languages and communication had not mixed.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن بينهم وبين بقية سكان الأرض غير يأجوج ومأجوج براري شاسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their poor grasp of others' speech may reflect little exposure from remote, non-temperate lands, or another cause.
rows.anchor: لقلة حفظهم لخروج بلادهم عن حد الاعتدال , أو لغير ذلك

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Their reading presents the people as scarcely making others understand them, shifting the direction of the communication difficulty.
rows.anchor: وذلك معنى قراءة حمزة والكسائي بضم التحتانية وكسر القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers may have been interpreters, nearby neighbors who knew some of their language, or people communicating by gesture.
rows.anchor: أي مترجموهم أو جيرانهم - الذين من دونهم - كما في مصحف ابن مسعود ممن يعرف بعض كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog are two human tribes descended from Japheth and so formidable that their threat cannot be extinguished.
rows.anchor: وهما قبيلتان من الناس من أولاد يافث , لا يطاق أمرهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report about the summons to the Fire states that Gog and Magog descend from Adam.
rows.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح في حديث بعث النار أنهم من ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their corruption encompasses many kinds of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: مفسدون في الأرض } بأنواع الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary reading of kharj means a payment the people would give Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة الجماعة , وزاد حمزة والكسائي ألفان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view treats kharj and kharaj as synonyms; another distinguishes a voluntary gift from an obligatory levy.
rows.anchor: فقيل : هما بمعنى واحد , وقيل : بل الخرج ما تبرعت به , والخراج بالألف ما لزمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They asked him to block all accessible land between them and Gog and Magog with a barrier, using the power God had granted him.
rows.anchor: من الأرض التي يمكن توصلهم إلينا منها بما آتاك الله من المكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn answers with restraint and piety that God's provision of capability is better than their payment.
rows.anchor: قال } بعفة وديانة وقصد للخير : { ما مكني

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the nun in makkannī distinctly, while the others assimilate it; the author links this to the outward and inward aspects of his capability.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير بإظهار النون في { مكنني } وغيره بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn asks for tools and workers, since local people know what suits their terrain while his forces are equipped for fighting.
rows.anchor: { فأعينوني بقوة } أي آلات وعمال أتقوى بها في فعل ذلكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A radm is a tightly interlocking, fortified obstruction, stronger than a simple barrier.
rows.anchor: حاجزا حصينا موثقا بعضه فوق بعض , مع التلاصق المتلاحم

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the foundation was dug to water, packed with stone, and coated with poured molten copper, forming a vein beneath the mountain.
rows.anchor: فحفر له الأساس حتى بلغ الماء وجعل حشوه الضخر وطينه النحاس يذاب فيصب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of āttūnī means give me; another means come to me, after which the command urges them to bring iron blocks.
rows.anchor: بفتح الهمزة بعدها ساكنة , ومدها على قراءة أي أعطوني وبهمزة وصل

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi describes alternating iron pieces and wood laid over the foundation until the gap was filled.
rows.anchor: فلم يزل يجعل قطع الحديد على الحطب والحطب على الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ṣadaf are the facing upper ends of the mountain clefts, named for their opposition and proximity across the construction.
rows.anchor: أعلى منقطع الجبلين الموصوفين , سميا لتصادفهما - أي تقابلهما وتقاربهما - بالبناء

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Their fatha reading of ṣadafayn signals the mountains' very straight alignment, like a wall with a doorway.
rows.anchor: قراءة من فتح الصاد والدال - وهم نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم - دالة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Their damma reading signals that the structure is exceptionally strong, with its upper and lower parts equally substantial.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو وابن عامر بضمهما دالة على أنه مع ذلك في غاية القوة

rows.speaker: شعبة عن عاصم
rows.claim: Shuʿba's damma with a still dal indicates the most stable and perfected construction, resistant to wind or weakness on either side.
rows.anchor: وقراءة شعبة عن عاصم بالضم وإسكان الدال على أشد ثبات وأتقنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The workers blow into bellows until the iron catches fire; molten copper is then poured over the heated iron.
rows.anchor: { انفخوا } في الأكوار فنفخوا فأضرم فيه النار , واستمر كذلك

rows.speaker: حمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: For qitr, they read a hamza with sukun, while the remaining readers use a lengthened, open hamza meaning give me copper.
rows.anchor: هذا في قراءة حمزة وأبي بكر عن عاصم بإسكان الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The copper and iron fuse into a solid mountain-like mass.
rows.anchor: ففعلوا ذلك فاختلط والتصق بعضه ببعض وصار جبلا صلدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot climb the wall because it is tall and smooth, or tunnel through it because it is thick, hard, and fused into one alloy.
rows.anchor: لثخنه وصلابته , وزيادة التاء هنا تدل على أن العلو عليه أصعب من نقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added ta in the longer verb marks climbing as harder than tunneling through the tall, tightly fused wall.
rows.anchor: وزيادة التاء هنا تدل على أن العلو عليه أصعب من نقبه

rows.speaker: ابن خرداذبه
rows.claim: Ibn Khurdadhbih reports that Salam the interpreter, sent by al-Wathiq to see the barrier, described its height as extending beyond sight.
rows.anchor: حكى ابن خرداذبه عن سلام الترجمان الذي أرسله أمير المؤمنين الواثق إليه حتى رآه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building stairs or piling earth would not help because they could not descend the far side; this fits their later escape by breaching it, not climbing over.
rows.anchor: لو احتالوا ببناء درج من جانبهم أو وضع تراب حتى ظهروا عليه لم ينفعهم ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that Gog and Magog dig daily until near sunrise, then leave; the barrier restores itself until, at the appointed end, their leader says God willing and they return to find it as left, breach it, and emerge.
rows.anchor: إن يأجوج ومأجوج ليحفرن السد كل يوم حتى إذا كادوا يرون شعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: زينب بنت جحش
rows.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Zaynab reports the Prophet showing that a small opening had been made in the barrier.
rows.anchor: في حديث الصحيحين عن زينب بنت جحش رضي الله عنها عن النبي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Ṣaḥīḥayn version from Abu Hurayra specifies that the opening was about the size of a ring made with the fingers.
rows.anchor: وفيه : ( مثل هذا وعقد تسعين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn calls the barrier a mercy because God enabled him to build it and thereby prevented corruption.
rows.anchor: المحسن إلي بإقداري عليه ومنع الفساد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Hour approaches, God will make the barrier flat by enabling Gog and Magog to breach and demolish it.
rows.anchor: بإقدراهم على نقبه وهدمه وتسهيل ذلك عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised release, their passage across the earth and ensuing corruption, and the Hour are all certain.
rows.anchor: في خروج يأجوج ومأجوج واختراقهم الأرض وإفسادهم لها ثم قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits a report of a man, elsewhere identified as from Medina, who told the Prophet that he had seen the barrier and was asked to describe it.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من أهل المدينة قال : يا رسول الله ! قد رأيت

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The witness described the barrier as striped like embroidered cloth, with red and black bands; variants call the stripes iron and copper, or say the land knew only iron.
rows.anchor: كالبرد المحبر : طريقة سوداء وطريقة حمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar is cited as documenting these versions from al-Tabari, Ibn Abi ʿUmar, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bazzar, including a route through Abu Bakra.
rows.anchor: رواه الطبري وابن أبي عمر والطبراني في مسند الشاميين وابن مردويه عنه والبزار

rows.speaker: شهربراز
rows.claim: In a report at the barrier, Shahrbaraz tells ʿAbd al-Rahman b. Rabiʿa that he sent a scout years earlier with funds, letters, and gifts through successive rulers to investigate the wall.
rows.anchor: إني بعثته منذ سنين نحو السد لينظر لي ما حاله ومن دونه

rows.speaker: مطر بن ثلج التميمي
rows.claim: The returning scout says a local ruler sent a falconer and eagle; at the wall he saw two mountains joined by a barrier rising above them and a black trench below.
rows.anchor: إذا جبلان بينهما سد مسدود حتى ارتفع على الجبلين بعد ما استوى بهما

rows.speaker: مطر بن ثلج التميمي
rows.claim: The falconer explains that each new king offers his finest worldly possession to God in a fire; he retrieves a piece of meat with a ruby in the eagle's talons and gives it to the scout.
rows.anchor: لا يلي ملك بعد ملك إلا تقرب إلى الله تعالى بأفضل ما عنده من الدنيا

rows.speaker: شهربراز
rows.claim: Shahrbaraz says the ruby is worth more than the city of Bab and that Arabs who keep faith, or whose supreme ruler does, cannot be overcome; the Persians would have confiscated it.
rows.anchor: هذه خير من هذه البلدة - يعني الباب - وايم الله ! لأنتم أحب إلي من آل كسرى

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن ربيعة
rows.claim: Asked to describe the barrier, the scout likens it to the striped garment of Maṭar b. Thalj; ʿAbd al-Rahman confirms that the report is accurate and recites the iron verse.
rows.anchor: هذا الثوب الذي على هذا الرجل , وأشار إلى مطر بن ثلج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories of the Sleepers and Dhul-Qarnayn, inserted between Moses's story and the signs of the Hour, answer Jewish challenges: accepting them binds the questioners, while rejecting them exposes their obstinacy.
rows.anchor: دال من قصة موسى عليه السلام على قيام الساعة فصار كله أعظم ملزم لهم أن قبلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter answers the questions eloquently while interweaving admonition, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, encouragement, warning, and rebuke of those concealing known truth.
rows.anchor: على أحسن وجه في أبلغ سياق وأبدع تناسب , وأدرج في خلاله ما أدرج من التذكير والوعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close reflects a wise, capable God who is neither impatient nor fatigued and describes the Hour through the final destinations of both groups.
rows.anchor: صنع القادر الحكيم الذي لا يستخفه ضجر فيستعجل , ولا يعيبه أمر فيستمهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the promise arrives, God will flatten the barrier by His power, release Gog and Magog after the Antichrist's emergence, and let them spread among people.
rows.anchor: جعلناه بقدرتنا التي نؤتيها ليأجوج ومأجوج دكاء فأخرجناهم على الناس بعد خروج الدجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means those behind and in front of the barrier will surge against one another like waves, devastating what they pass except what God wills.
rows.anchor: كما يموج البحر , فأهلكوا ما مروا عليه من شيء إلا ما اراد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will then destroy Gog and Magog and, soon after, all creatures.
rows.anchor: ثم أبادهم الذي خلقهم وبقرب ذلك أفنى الخلائق أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet may refer to the second blast, since the next clause says the people were gathered.
rows.anchor: الثانية لقوله : { فجمعناهم } ويجوز أن تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an understood sequence has the first blast kill all creatures and dissolve their bodies, then the second resurrect and gather them from scattered remains.
rows.anchor: أو وانفخ في الصور فمات الخلائق كلهم , فبليت أجسامهم , وتفتت عظامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection gathers everyone at once, as quickly as an eye-blink, to the assembly for reckoning and punishment or reward.
rows.anchor: فأقمناهم دفعة واحدة كلمح البصر , وحشرناهم إلى الموقف للحساب ثم العقاب أو الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is displayed openly with all its terrors to the gathered disbelievers, who can find no way to turn aside.
rows.anchor: ظاهرا لهم كل ما فيها من الأهوال وهم لا يجدون عنها مصرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' inner and outward eyes are veiled from remembrance: they ignore worldly adornment as a sign of the Hour, which will be destroyed and recreated.
rows.anchor: أعينهم } الوجهية و القلبية { في غطاء عن ذكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to hear means they lack the capacity that would benefit them, because weak minds are submerged in frivolity; this rebuke exceeds merely denying sight or hearing.
rows.anchor: وهو أبلغ في التبكيت بالغباوة والتقريع بالبلادة من مجرد نفي البصر والسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question rebukes those who assume God's living servants, such as angels, Ezra, or Jesus, and dead idols can be protectors apart from Him.
rows.anchor: { عبادي } من الأحياء كالملائكة وعزير والمسيح , والأموات كالأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They take these beings as protectors without God's permission; the omitted object is that they will defend, protect, provide offspring, or spare them punishment.
rows.anchor: { حسب } محذوف تقديرهك ينصرونهم ويدفعون عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means they cannot expect their chosen guardians to prevent divine punishment; instead Hell has been prepared as the disbelievers' lodging.
rows.anchor: { إنا اعتدنا جهنم } التي تقدم أنا عرضناها لهم { للكافرين نزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene reverses worldly preferences: disbelievers then beg to leave, while believers had longed to depart this world for their Lord.
rows.anchor: وذلك عكس ما كان في الدنيا من ركون الكفار إليها , ومحبتهم في طول البقاء فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After answering the questions with proofs and resolving the dispute, the passage turns to resurrection, the neglected issue behind their disbelief.
rows.anchor: وأتبع ذلك بقص الأمر الذي بإغفاله تجرؤوا على الكفر , وهو أمر البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse closes inquiry because God's knowledge and the uncountable blessings of Paradise have no limit, so no complete account of His knowledge or gifts is possible.
rows.anchor: معلوماته لا تحد , لأن مقدوراته في تنعيم أهل الجنة لا آخر لها فلا تعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews answered the earlier statement that human knowledge is slight by claiming they had the Torah; their questions nevertheless entail matters with lengthy, formidable explanations.
rows.anchor: وكان اليهود قد اعترضوا على قوله في أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea is finite and would run out as ink before God's words, since created beings are contingent while His attributes and knowledge are necessary and boundless.
rows.anchor: المخلوقات - لكونها ممكنة - ليس لها من ذاتها إلا العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even equal additional seas would be exhausted; the impossible comparison is a rhetorical way to say God's words do not end, and plural wording magnifies the immense supply.
rows.anchor: هذا كله كناية عن عدم النفاد , لأنه تعليق على محال عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the sea runs out before God's words closes questioning; a different construction could invite sophistry by treating the words as limited only during the comparison.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك كاف في قطعهم عن الاستقصاء في السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing in this verse and Luqman is each most eloquent for its own context; neither explicitly says God's words end, and their contexts show that they do not.
rows.anchor: فما في كل سورة أبلغ بالنسبة إلى سياقه , مع أنه ليس في إفصاح واحدة منهما ما يدل على نفاد الكلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may appear ambiguous, but a phrase within a negation does not entail existence; the decisive proof is that God and His attributes have no end.
rows.anchor: من أن ما في حيز السلب لا يقتضي الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to demands for exhaustive answers and objections that the Prophet is human while stones may be gods, the command says his delay was not from incapacity, ignorance, or low standing.
rows.anchor: ما لك لا تحدثنا من هذه الكلمات بكل ما نسألك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is human and has no independent power to create or disclose the unseen; his prophethood follows God's established practice with earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: لا أمر لي ولا قدرة إلا على ما يقدرني عليه ربي , ولا استبعاد لرسالتي من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation's essential message is that God alone is divine, indivisible, all-powerful, and without rival; the questions about the Spirit and stories are secondary.
rows.anchor: أي لاينقسم بمجانسة ولا غيرها , قادر على ما يريد , لا منازع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Prophet lets people know the peripheral answers as faith in the unseen now, then as certainty by witnessing after death; otherwise knowing them brings no benefit.
rows.anchor: وإن اتبعتموني علمتموه الآن وما دل عليه من أمر الساعة إيمانا بالغيب علم اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope of meeting the Lord includes belief in recompense and vision, and recognition that He alone creates, provides, owns, and commands His servants.
rows.anchor: يؤمن بمجازاته له على أعماله في الآخرة برؤيته وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because recompense matches deeds, a servant must perform sincere, sound religious acts, including faith and bodily, inward, and financial duties, without even ostentatious association.
rows.anchor: كان الجزاء من جنس العمل , كان الواجب على العبد الإخلاص في عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the opening's themes of God's words and revelation, then calls to exclusive worship, good works, glad tidings for believers, and warning for those who turn away.
rows.anchor: وقد انطبق آخر السورة على أولها بوصف كلمات الله ثم ما يوحى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam follows the surah describing the Book's complete straightness and opens with disjoint letters, echoing the pattern of earlier surahs associated with guidance and divine favors.
rows.anchor: افتتحها بالأحرف المقطعة , كما افتتح السورة التي تلي أم الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five opening letters correspond to five related surahs and their themes: encompassing favors, the Book, and the first and later acts of creation.
rows.anchor: وهي خمسة أحرف على عددها مع تلك السور , وهي جامعة النعم , وواصفة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr introduces the account being recited: God's mercy to His servant Zakariyya, including support, answered prayer, and granting what he sought.
rows.anchor: { ذكر } أي هذا الذي أتلوه عليكم ذكر { رحمت ربك } أي المحسن إليك بالتأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya is identified as son of Mathan; God's mercy rewards his monotheism and righteous work guided by hope of meeting his Lord.
rows.anchor: زكريا * } أي ابن ماثان , جزاء له على توحيده وعمله الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His hidden prayer suits the intimacy of a close lover's private address to the beloved; God nevertheless knows even the most secret plea.
rows.anchor: كما يفعل المحب القريب مع حبيبه المقبل عليه في قصد خطاب السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God simply Lord without a vocative particle signals extreme closeness.
rows.anchor: { قال رب } بحذف الأداة للدلالة على غاية القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular bone is the body's strongest support, so its weakening implies greater weakness throughout; a plural would suggest only all the bones collectively.
rows.anchor: { العظم مني } أي هذا الجنس الذي هو أقوى ما في بدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of the head igniting with gray hair rhetorically depicts the spread of old age.
rows.anchor: { واشتعل الرأس } أي شعره مني { شيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya says his earlier prayers never left him disappointed and asks again on the basis of God's customary generosity.
rows.anchor: { بدعائك } أي بدعائي إياك { رب شقيا * } فأجرني في هذه المرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His request is both gratitude and appeal: God previously granted a remotely improbable favor to Abraham's father as well, and kindness builds on earlier kindness.
rows.anchor: فإن المحسن يربي أول إحسانه بآخره وإن كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya fears relatives will mishandle his legacy after his death; his barren wife leaves him no ordinary hope of a child, so he appeals to God's extraordinary provision.
rows.anchor: { وإني خفت الموالي } أي فعل الأقارب أن يسيئوا الخلافة { من وراءي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks for an heir from God's hidden and extraordinary gifts, since ordinary causes for a child are absent.
rows.anchor: { من لدنك } أي من الأمور المستبطنة المستغربة التي عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks for a son from his own line who will inherit his knowledge, prophethood, and work, and further inherit the virtues and gifts bestowed on Jacob's family.
rows.anchor: { يرثني } في جميع ما أنا فيه من العلم والنبوة والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes Jacob's family to recall God's promise to complete His favor on Joseph and Jacob's household, and notes Israel became the name of all the tribes.
rows.anchor: وخص اسم يعقوب اقتداء به نفسه إذ قال ليوسف عليهما الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: القاضي العضد
rows.claim: Al-Qadi al-ʿAḍud objects that reading yarith as an adjective makes the prayer unanswered, since Yahya was killed during his father's life and an heir succeeds after death.
rows.anchor: كون { يرث } على قراءة الرفع صفة بأنه يلزم عليه عدم إجابة دعائه

rows.speaker: القاضي العضد
rows.claim: Al-Qadi al-ʿAḍud resolves the grammatical problem by making yarith an independent clause, leaving only a mistaken expectation by Zakariyya.
rows.anchor: قال : فتجعل استئنافية , ولا يلزم حينئذ إلا خلف ظنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects attributing a false expectation to Zakariyya and says no prayer goes unanswered if the report of Yahya's earlier death is authentic.
rows.anchor: وأنا أجله عن ذلك , لأنه لا يلزم تخلف دعائه ولا يتجرأ على علي مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Yahya died first, inheritance of knowledge during his father's life is a valid metaphor for what it later becomes, as in the Prophet's saying that scholars inherit prophets.
rows.anchor: كان تسمية العلم الذي أخذه عنه في حياته إرثا مجازا مرسلا باعتبار ما يؤول إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Yahya died before Zakariyya, behind me can mean beyond my sight: the aging prophet feared relatives would act badly when outside his supervision.
rows.anchor: وخفت سوء فعلهم إذا خرجوا من عندي وغابوا عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If that death report is not authentic, the objection disappears; old chronologies derived from Jews are worthless.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يصح موته قبله بالطريق المذكور لم يصح أصلا , وينتفي الاعتراض رأسا

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says Babylonian forces killed Yahya and then slaughtered thousands of Israelites over his still-boiling blood, which would not stop.
rows.anchor: فذبح منهم بيوزردان على ذلك الدم سبعمائة وسبعين رجلا من رؤوسهم فلم يهدأ

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: In al-Baghawi's account, the Israelites confess that the blood is Yahya's and that they killed him; the commander prays, the blood stops, and he professes belief, then fills a trench with livestock and earlier corpses to deceive the Babylonian king about the slaughter.
rows.anchor: إن هذا دم بني كانوا ينهانا عن أمور كثيرة من سخط الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes this account to show Yahya survived his father, and adds earlier Gospel-based evidence cited in the discussion of Al ʿImran.
rows.anchor: فهذا كما ترى ظاهر في أن يحيى تخلف بعد أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya asks that his son remain pleasing to God and meet Him in that state.
rows.anchor: { رضيا * } أي بعين الرضا منك دائما حتى يلقاك على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers his prayer with a glad announcement; the doubled form of the verb, used by all except Hamza, better emphasizes news so extraordinary it might be denied.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الجماعة غير حمزة بالتشديد أوفق من قراءة حمزة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The child is named Yahya, a name not previously bestowed; the author says this name was reserved as an honor for him.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفه بما عرف به أن مما شرفه به أن ادخر له هذا اتلاسم فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya asks how he can have a son and seeks confirmation, curious about the circumstances rather than doubting the truthful promise or speaking rashly.
rows.anchor: { قال } عالما بصدقها طالبا لتأكيدها , والتلذيذ بترديدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is astonishing because his wife had been barren even when young and both are now old, while a ghulam suggests full masculine strength.
rows.anchor: غير قابلة للولد عادة وأنا وهي شابان فلم يأتنا ولد لاختلال أحد السبيبن

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that Zakariyya was 120 and his wife 98.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كان ابن عشرين ومائة سنة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says Zakariyya may be asking whether God will grant a child despite their condition or rejuvenate him; God works through ordinary causes or sheer power, known only to the perceptive.
rows.anchor: إن هذا على الاستخبار أيعطيه الله الولد بتلك الحال أم يقلبه شابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says creating Yahya under these conditions is easy for Him, with no distinction in difficulty between this and any other creation.
rows.anchor: { علي } أي خاصة { هين } لافرق عندي بينه وبين غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya's own creation from nothing is an even clearer proof that God can create his son from the aging couple.
rows.anchor: { وقد خلقتك } أي قدرتك وصورتك وأوجدتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened takū form emphasizes that humans possess no existence of their own, only prior nonbeing.
rows.anchor: بحذف النون وليثبت أنه ليس له من ذاته إلا العدم المحض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya requests a confirming sign; he will be unable to speak with people for three nights despite being physically sound, while remaining able to worship and converse with God and other righteous beings.
rows.anchor: { سويا * } من غير خرس ولا مرض ولا حبسة عن مطلق الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night wording fits the surah's theme of mercy, since night is when mercy descends, while the parallel Al ʿImran wording counts days.
rows.anchor: ولما بدئت السور بالرحمة , وكان الليل محل تنزلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Silence toward people while continuing remembrance marks his sincerity and complete devotion to God.
rows.anchor: وجعلت الآية الدالة عليه سكوتا عن غير ذكر الله دلالة على إخلاصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miḥrāb is the front and most honored part of the temple; Zakariyya emerged from it able to praise God but unable to speak to people.
rows.anchor: من المحراب } الذي كان فيه وهو صدر الهيكل وأشرف ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He conveyed the instruction to glorify God morning and evening by lip movement without speech.
rows.anchor: فأوحى إليهم } أي أشار بشفتيه من غير نطق

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says ramz is principally a lip gesture, though it can also be a movement of brows, eyes, or hands; its root sense is motion.
rows.anchor: والرمز : الإيماء بالشفتين , وقد يستعمل في الإيماء بالحاجبين والعينين واليدين

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari likewise says lip gestures are the usual Arabic sense of ramz, with eye, brow, or hand gestures less common, and cites Mujahid for moving the lips here.
rows.anchor: وأما الرمز فإن الأغلب من معانيه عند العرب الإيماء بالشفتين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets Zakariyya's signal as movement of the lips.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به هنا تحرك الشفتين عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because waḥy can mean gesture, allusion, or quiet speech, the signal may have taken any of those forms, while Zakariyya spoke fluently to God.
rows.anchor: وهو ظاهر أيضا في الوحي لأنه مطلق الإشارة والكناية والكلام الخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥ means producing God's transcendence and sanctification through prayer and other worship.
rows.anchor: { أن سبحوا } أي أوجدوا التنزيه والتقديس لله تعالى بالصلاة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya is told to take up the Torah firmly and is granted judgment, understood as Torah knowledge, in childhood.
rows.anchor: { الحكم } أي البنوة والفهم للتوراة { صبيا * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving prophethood before maturity is extraordinary because that charge normally requires fully developed reason and strength.
rows.anchor: لما كانت النبوة لا يستضلع بأمرها ويقوى على حملها إلا عند استحكام العقل ببلوغ الأشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's people were not given this sign because they lacked a prior prophetic community whose denial would contradict their own history; his established truthfulness and enduring Qur'anic miracle served that role.
rows.anchor: فعوض أعظم من ذلك بغرائز الصدق التي أوجبت له تسميته بالأمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants Yahya tenderness, reverence, gentleness of heart, provision, and blessing directly from Himself, without teaching or experience.
rows.anchor: { حنانا } أي رحمة وهيبة ووقارا ورقة قلب ورزقا وبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His zakāh is purity of intention that flows into his words and actions; piety is his natural disposition.
rows.anchor: { وزكاة } أي طهارة في نيته تفيض على أفعاله وأقواله { وكان } أي جبلة وطبعا { تقيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya is broadly good to his parents and others, with no tyrannical or disobedient disposition; the negation concerns his innate character, not firmness toward those deserving it.
rows.anchor: { وبرا } أي واسع الأخلاق محسنا { بوالديه ولم يكن } جبلة وطبعا { جبارا } عليهما ولا على غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic form describes the negated tyrannical and disobedient traits as innate; lesser faults may be removed by purification of the heart.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بصيغة المبالغة يفهم أن المنفي الجبل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace protects Yahya from religious harm at birth, the distress of death and what follows, and every fear after resurrection; the three moments are the hardest, so safety then entails safety elsewhere.
rows.anchor: من كل سوء يلحق بالولادة وما بعدها في شيء من أمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests the greeting is indefinite because Yahya was killed and his body was not preserved in peace, unlike Jesus in the following passage.
rows.anchor: ولعله نكر السلام لأنه قتل فما سلم بدنه بخلاف ما يأتي في عيسى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says every child of Adam meets God with a sin and may be punished or forgiven, except Yahya, described as noble, chaste, prophetic, and righteous; the Prophet indicates that his remembrance is tiny as a speck.
rows.anchor: كل بني آدم يلقى الله يوم القيامة بذنب وقد يعذبه عليه إن شاء أو يرحمه إلا يحيى بن زكريا

rows.speaker: الهيثمي
rows.claim: Al-Haythami grades the Abu Hurayra report as having Hajjaj b. Sulayman, whom Ibn Hibban and others trusted while Abu Zurʿa and others weakened; the remaining narrators are trustworthy.
rows.anchor: وفيه حجاج ابن سليمان الرعيني وثقه ابن حبان وغيره وضعفه أبو زرعة وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas's version says no one should be better than Yahya; the Prophet cites the Qur'anic descriptions, including that he never committed or intended a sin.
rows.anchor: ما ينبغي أن يكون أحد خيرا من يحيى بن زكريا

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar also transmits the virtue report; its chain includes ʿAli b. Zayd b. Judʿan, weakened by most critics though some approved him, while the others are trustworthy.
rows.anchor: ورواه أيضا البزار وفيه على بن زيد بن جدعان ضعفه الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of human development refute claims that God has a child: both child and parent depend on need, incompatible with divine independence.
rows.anchor: من حيث إن ذلك قاض على الولد نفسه وعلى أبيه بالحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's story follows Yahya's: his birth came through causes nearly null because of the couple's age and barrenness, while Mary's story has no male cause at all, showing God creates through strong, weak, or no causes and needs no child.
rows.anchor: أتبعه بقصة هي أغرب من قصته بكونها ليس فيها إلا سبب واحد وهو المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews who challenged the Arabs about these stories deserved rebuke for not warning them about their idolatry; Yahya's death at Jewish hands especially indicts them, and his story prepares the case for Jesus.
rows.anchor: قصة زكريا أعظم في تبكيتهم بمباشرتهم لقتله وقتل ولده يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative obliges Jews to recognize Jesus and Christians to recognize him as God's servant; Yahya and Jesus shared miraculous births, era, and close kinship, witnessed by both disputing groups.
rows.anchor: إلزاما لهم بالاعتراف به , وللنصارى بالاعتراف بأنه عبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya's story is preferred before Isaac's because of the preceding argument and because contemporaries of Jesus witnessed the intertwined lives of Yahya and Jesus; Jesus's more unusual story changes the style.
rows.anchor: وكانت قصة يحيى أولى من قصة إسحاق عليهما السلام لما تقدم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن مالك بن صعصعة
rows.claim: In the sound Miʿraj report, the Prophet identifies Yahya and Jesus as maternal cousins; the author uses it to call Mary Yahya's maternal aunt.
rows.anchor: في الصحيح من حديث أنس بن مالك عن مالك بن صعصعة الأنصاري رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew herself from her family to an eastern place, whose direction symbolizes the divine light soon to reach her.
rows.anchor: { مكانا شرقيا * } عن مكانهم , فكان انفرادها في جهة مطالع الأنوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She placed a screen close to her family, perhaps to bathe or for another reason, and God sent Gabriel to announce the honor of Jesus's birth without a father so she would not despair.
rows.anchor: أي أدنى مكان في مكانهم لانفرادها للا غتسال أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel, a spirit, took visible human form; he appeared well-proportioned and handsome to lessen her fear.
rows.anchor: أي تشبح وهو روحاني بصورة الجسماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's refuge in the Merciful shows firm devotion and confidence that God protects her; invoking His universal mercy also suits her special favor.
rows.anchor: ربي الذي رحمته عامة لجميع عباده في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She senses Gabriel's piety and says if he is God-fearing, urging him to act consistently with her plea.
rows.anchor: بما أنار الله من بصيرتها وأصفى من سريرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel reassures her that he is not suspect but a messenger of the Lord she invoked; the name Lord emphasizes kindness and the surah's theme of mercy.
rows.anchor: أي فأنا لست متهما , متصف بما ذكرت وزيادة الرسلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For la-ahaba, one reading has Gabriel say he will give by God's command, while another has God as the giver; fronting the phrase builds anticipation.
rows.anchor: بأمره أو ليهب هو على القراءة الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised ghulam is a male child of great strength and maturity, pure from impurity and growing in goodness and blessing.
rows.anchor: { غلاما } أي ولدا ذكرا في غايىة القوة والرجولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary denies any sexual contact, whether lawful marriage, illicit sex, or an ambiguous case, and denies ever being a prostitute.
rows.anchor: { ولم يمسسني بشر } بنكاح أصلا حلال ولا غيره بشبهة ولا غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She speaks with urgency and omits the nun in akū to give emphatic force to her denial.
rows.anchor: فأوجزت حتى بحذف النون من ( كان ) ولتفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word baghiy denotes a woman given to sexual wrongdoing; the feminine baghiya is avoided because the form is conventional like ḥāʾiḍ and ʿāqir and would suggest one actively engaged in it.
rows.anchor: ولم يأت ( بغية ) لغلبة إيقاعه على النساء , فكان مثل حائض وعاقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel confirms that events will occur exactly as promised; God's Lord-name, rather than the divine name used in Al ʿImran, suits this surah's mercy theme.
rows.anchor: عبر باسم الرب الذي صدرت به بخلاف سورة التوحيد آل عمران المصدرة بالاسم الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's conception is a sign of resurrection and completes the four modes of human creation: from woman alone, man alone, neither, or both.
rows.anchor: وبه تمام القسمة الراعية في خلق البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is mercy for believers in his time and for most people through faith and rescue from trials near the end; unlike Salih's she-camel, his sign does not destroy rejecters.
rows.anchor: لا كآية صالح عليه السلام لأنها كانت آية استئصال لأهل الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree is settled and easy, with no obstacle; pregnancy follows immediately by the process described elsewhere.
rows.anchor: محكوما به مبتوتا هو في غاية السهولة لا مانع منه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel breathed through the opening of Mary's garment and the breath reached her womb, causing conception.
rows.anchor: فنفخ في درعها فوصل النفخ إلى جوفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequential fa marks her immediate withdrawal with the child in her womb to a remote place, away from family or the eastern location.
rows.anchor: { فانتبذت به } أي فاعتزلت - وهو في بطنها - حالة { مكانا قصيا * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next fa signals labor soon after conception; the pains compelled her to the trunk, meaning the part of the palm above ground and below its branches.
rows.anchor: { فأجاءها } أي فأتى بها وألجأها { المخاض } وهو تحرك الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite palm is presented as the only tree in that cold region, remarkable because palms poorly tolerate cold; its male pollination and fruit make it apt as a sign of conception without a father and nourishment for childbirth.
rows.anchor: لأنها لا تحمل إلا بإلقاح من ذكور النخل , فحملها بمجرد هزها أنسب شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing disgrace, Mary wishes she had died and become an entirely forgotten nonentity.
rows.anchor: لما حصل عندها من خوف العار : { ياليتني مت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus calls to Mary from beneath her and tells her not to grieve.
rows.anchor: { فناداها من تحتها } وهو عيسى عليه السلام { ألا تحزني

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the miraculous pregnancy and birth lasted an hour rather than passing through stages of formation from seed.
rows.anchor: صح أن مدة حملها له وولادته ساعة لأنه كان مبدعا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir adds that people would have objected to the pregnancy if they had witnessed it, and that this objection would have been transmitted just as the objection to the birth was.
rows.anchor: ونقله ابن كثير وقال : صلى الله عليه وسلم أنهم أنكروا عليها زمن الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sary beneath her is a stream of water in a land without flowing water, a sign that should comfort her.
rows.anchor: جدولا من الماء جليلا آية لك تطيب نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is told to shake the thick trunk; the directive redirects her thoughts from grief even though a dry tree out of season should not yield fruit.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقصود التهويل لصرف فكرها عما دهمها من الهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fresh ripe dates fall in abundance, comforting her and demonstrating her innocence through an extraordinary sign.
rows.anchor: { رطبا جنيا * } طريا آية أخرى عظيمة تطيب النفس وتذهب بالحزن

rows.speaker: قراءة الجماعة وحمزة
rows.claim: Their tafāʿul reading indicates dates fall from a palm that should not fruit, making the occurrence a clear supernatural sign.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بصيغة التفاعل في قراءة لاجماعة وحمزة للدلالة علىأن التمر يسقط منها

rows.speaker: قراءة الجماعة
rows.claim: The assimilated reading also suggests it is almost hidden that the dates came from the dry palm, which had not borne fruit.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الجماعة بالإدغام تشير مع ذلك إلى أنه مع شدته يكاد أن يخفي كونه منها

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza's open, light reading points to the ease and abundance of the dates' falling.
rows.anchor: وقراءة حمزة بالفتح والتخفيف تشير إلى سهولة تساقطه وكثرته

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hafs's damma and qaf-kasra form denotes abundance and makes Mary's role in the falling explicit.
rows.anchor: وقراءة حفص عن عاصم بالضم وكسر القاف من فاعل , تدل على الكثرة
